A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Denoising as Adaptation work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original denoising, deraining and deblurring experiments, component ablations and architecture-scaling results in Tables 1–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds training-dynamics, diffusion-capacity and restoration-backbone results, including Figure A10 and Table A3.

M1.justification: The diffusion-guided training, channel shuffling, residual-swapping contrastive learning and unpaired extension are retained. v3 names the average of the diffusion and contrastive losses LDif before rewriting Equation 4, preserving the objective. Algorithms 1–2 document the existing training and inference procedure.

E1.justification: The same restoration tasks and synthetic, real-world and unpaired training datasets remain. SIDD, SPA, RealBlur-J, DND and Real-Internet were already evaluated in v2. Additional architecture tests and failure illustrations remain within this restoration and domain-shift coverage.

E2.justification: Figures A6–A7 add DANN and MaskedD to the existing DND visual comparisons, and Figure A8 adds Restormer on Real-Internet. Figure 5 replaces the deraining panel labeled Vanilla with Input. The comparator sets in the main quantitative tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments compare three diffusion-network channel configurations, track training with L1 versus L1 plus diffusion loss, and evaluate adaptation with DnCNN, Restormer and SwinIR. These extend experimental configurations and controls; the retained benchmark settings, preprocessing and metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections A4.5–A4.6 substantially extend the analyses with challenging-image failure cases, validation trajectories testing overfitting during training, and a diffusion-capacity study. Figures A9–A10 address failure conditions and the behavior and capacity requirements of the training proxy beyond v2's retained component and restoration-network ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run uncertainty. The added training curves and capacity bars do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 substantially extends reported outcomes while retaining all numerical results in Tables 1–5 and A1–A2. New Table A3 reports Vanilla/adapted SIDD PSNR of 25.98/30.46 for DnCNN, 24.10/33.98 for Restormer and 30.86/34.85 for SwinIR. Figures A9–A10 add failure, training and capacity findings; Figures 4–5 add per-image PSNR, and A6–A8 add comparator outputs.

T1.justification: No theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised. Equation 4 uses an equivalent combined-loss notation; the new information-guidance discussion is conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about noise-space adaptation, shortcut prevention, compatibility across restoration networks and no additional inference cost. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit limitations for strong and out-of-distribution degradation in A4.5, interprets diffusion-capacity requirements in A4.6, and explains guidance from synthetic clean targets in A5.2. The existing limitation concerning low-frequency blur remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 make model updates and one-pass inference explicit, Table 1 adds training-loss descriptions, and A4.6 specifies diffusion-network channel configurations, including the default [64, 128, 256, 512]. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained implementation or resource access.

R1.justification: v3 adds noise-modeling citations, Cai et al. (2021), and a substantive comparison with MAR (Li et al., 2024), distinguishing dense pixel restoration from token-level generation. It removes the Zhang et al. perceptual-metric reference. Publication updates for existing references do not change their identity or the central positioning.

P1.justification: The main text receives localized tightening and notation clarification. New appendix subsections explain the additional analyses and training procedure, and an acknowledgment and ICLR publication header are added. The main section order and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The visual comparison material is substantially expanded: Figures A6–A8 become multi-method galleries, Figures A9–A10 and Table A3 are added, and Algorithms 1–2 introduce procedural displays. Figures 4–5 gain PSNR annotations, Figure 5 changes its deraining crop, and Table 1 gains a training-loss row.

improvement.justification: v3 provides better support and transparency through diffusion-capacity and training-dynamics analyses, additional backbone results, explicit failure cases and clearer training documentation. These strengthen an already established empirical argument while preserving the core method and benchmark findings. The gains are useful but incremental; the failure comparison also leaves its comparator unnamed.
